ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 1993, Part 2 and sections 88, 91, 189, 194 and 195 (incorporation, name rules, registered office and registers); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, sections 10, 11, 12, 20, 21 and 22 read with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Definitions and Other Matters) Regulations 2018. There is no standalone public UBO decree; ultimate beneficial ownership is established through mandatory AML/CFT customer due diligence and corporate register data only accessible to competent authorities on request.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the New Zealand Consolidated Sanctions List, European Union financial sanctions lists, and domestic PEP databases as defined under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for each domestic or foreign politically exposed person, family member or close associate. Adverse media, criminal record and regulatory enforcement checks are also conducted before incorporation and before bank account opening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Company Register
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal company name must be capable of accurate presentation in Latin or Roman characters and must be searchable on the New Zealand Companies Register. Chinese ideographic characters are not accepted in the legal name; any Chinese trading style must be recorded through a separately registered trade mark or business name and all brand references in the legal name must follow the approved Latin transliteration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may amend the proposed name and file a fresh reservation online through the Companies Office portal. If the rejection arises from a prohibited or sensitive token, written consent from the relevant approving Minister or regulator must be obtained before re-filing. The applicant may request an administrative reconsideration through the Companies Office contact centre within 10 working days of the rejection notice. If the administrative review is unsuccessful, the applicant may appeal the Registrar's decision to the High Court of New Zealand under the Companies Act 1993, with notice to be filed within 20 working days of the final written decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not acceptable as the sole statutory registered office. The registered office must be a physical New Zealand street address capable of receiving service of process and official documents. A virtual office may be used only as a secondary administrative or marketing address; for a wholesale liquor export business, commercial substance is strengthened by a physical office, storage or bonded excise facility, and local management presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspection is approximately 10 to 15 percent annualized for a standard export wholesaler with a physical registered office and compliant excise arrangements. The risk increases above 30 percent where the registered office is a shared or residential address, where alcohol is stored without proper customs or excise approval, or where the company is part of a high-risk supply chain involving cash-intensive intermediaries.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No. 105), principally s. 10 (company name), s. 12 (registered office), ss. 11-19 (incorporation, requisition and certificate of incorporation), ss. 87-90 (share register and certificates), s. 122 (written resolutions), s. 128 (financial reporting), and s. 151 (requirement for at least one director resident in New Zealand or Australia), together with the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and the AML/CFT Act 2009 for entity compliance.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the New Zealand Companies Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 2 - Application for Incorporation of a Company, lodged electronically through the New Zealand Companies Register portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital; New Zealand law imposes no authorised capital, minimum capital, or escrow requirement. Shares may be issued at any subscription price, including nil or nominal paid-up value, provided that section 45 of the Companies Act 1993 (no issue at a discount) and the solvency test in section 52 are satisfied.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WRITTEN RESOLUTIONS OF THE SOLE SHAREHOLDER AND DIRECTOR OF NZ LTD. TAKEN PURSUANT TO SECTION 122 OF THE COMPANIES ACT 1993. 1. Allotment of Shares: It is resolved that the allotment of 1,000 fully paid ordinary shares at NZ$1.00 each to the founding shareholder, as stated in the Form 2 incorporation application, be ratified, and that the share register be maintained in accordance with sections 87-90 of the Act. 2. Registered Office: It is resolved that the registered office of the Company shall be situated at [physical New Zealand address], that the register of directors and other statutory records required by sections 189-190 of the Act shall be kept at that office, and that the address for service shall be the same. 3. Appointment of Officers: It is resolved that [Full Name of Director], a natural person resident in New Zealand, be and is hereby appointed as sole director of the Company; and that [Full Name] be appointed as Company Secretary and Compliance Officer with authority to complete export and liquor-licensing filings. 4. Banking and Signing Authority: It is resolved that the Company open a corporate bank account with a registered New Zealand bank, and that any one of the nominated signatories be empowered to sign cheques, SWIFT wire instructions, and letters of credit in the Company's name. 5. General: The foregoing resolutions shall be recorded in the Company's minute book and take immediate effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Pre-Incorporation Due Diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office / New Zealand Companies Register (online portal: companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Companies Register with a RealMe account and conduct an availability search. Reserve up to twenty proposed names for an initial period of twenty business days, ensuring the chosen name is not identical to an existing registered or reserved name and does not contravene sections 21 and 22 of the Companies Act 1993 by being offensive, misleading, or implying Crown, government, or official endorsement. Conduct a supplementary trademark search on the Intellectual Property Office of New Zealand (IPONZ) register for the proposed brand identifier and verify that the name is compatible with the wholesale export of high-proof baijiu spirits.
required_dossiers: Three proposed company names in order of preference
IPONZ trademark search report (recommended)
Full legal name, date of birth, and residential address of the proposed shareholder(s)
Identification documents of the proposed director(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar declines the name under section 23, respond in writing within the remaining reservation period proposing an alternative name or file a fresh reservation; an applicant whose name is declined may also request written reasons and seek judicial review, but the practical remedy is immediate re-submission with a distinguishing element, such as a geographic or branding discriptor.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Constitution and Statutory Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founder(s) and proposed director(s) of the company (private constituent act)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Elect to rely on the default constitution in the Fifth Schedule of the Companies Act 1993, or execute a custom constitution that complies with section 26 and does not contravene the mandatory provisions of the Act. Obtain signed consents from each person to act as director and from each shareholder to take the subscribed shares. Confirm that at least one director is a natural person resident in New Zealand or Australia as required by section 151(2A) of the Act. Retain original signed consents in the company's minute book and make digital copies available for electronic lodgement at incorporation.
required_dossiers: Signed custom constitution, if adopted
Signed consent to act as director (with director's full name, date of birth, and residential address)
Signed consent to become a shareholder
Share allotment schedule specifying class, number, and consideration per share
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar identifies a provision contrary to the Companies Act 1993, convene a special shareholder meeting to pass an amending special resolution under section 117, and thereafter re-file the constitution and any associated notices; alternatively, revert to the statutory default constitution in the Fifth Schedule.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgement of Form 2 Application for Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (online Companies Register)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 2 - Application for Incorporation electronically: enter the reserved company name, the maximum number and class of shares (e.g., 1,000 ordinary shares at NZ$1.00 each), the full legal names, dates of birth, and residential addresses of all directors, and the physical New Zealand address of the registered office together with the address for service. Attach the consents to act as director and shareholder. Declare compliance with the Companies Act 1993 and complete the AML/CFT verification questions. Pay the statutory NZ$150.00 filing fee by credit or debit card. Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation under section 14 of the Act and automatically allocates a New Zealand Business Number, both of which should be downloaded and certified for subsequent license and bank applications.
required_dossiers: Completed online Form 2 data set
Digital copy of director's signed consent to act
Digital copy of shareholder's signed consent to take shares
Proof of registered office address (title, lease, or owner's consent letter)
Certificate of name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition under section 19 of the Companies Act 1993, the applicant must remedy the stated defect within five working days by submitting an amended electronic filing and, if necessary, a statutory declaration clarifying the error; failure to remedy results in the application being deemed withdrawn and the fee forfeited, in which case a fresh Form 2 must be lodged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue and Tax Registrations (IRD, GST, PAYE, and Export Treatment)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (myIR online portal) under the Tax Administration Act 1994
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the issued New Zealand Business Number to establish the company's myIR account; the company is automatically registered for income tax. File an application for GST registration immediately, which is compulsory if projected annual turnover exceeds NZ$60,000 and is advisable notwithstanding, because export sales of goods are zero-rated under section 11(1)(a) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, enabling recovery of input credits on establishment costs. Register for PAYE if any New Zealand employees, directors' salaries, or shareholder-employee remuneration are contemplated. Confirm the company's status as a New Zealand tax resident and record the appropriate business activity code for wholesale liquor export.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
New Zealand Business Number certificate
Director's and shareholder's passport identification
Registered office lease or title deed
Business plan with a projected revenue and export turnover statement
Board resolution appointing the tax filing agent, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Inland Revenue Department queries the GST, PAYE, or income tax registration, respond through myIR with a letter of explanation and supporting transaction documents; any late-filing or late-payment penalty may be remitted under section 183A of the Tax Administration Act 1994 on grounds of reasonable cause, provided the corrective return is filed promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Share Allotment Minuting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered New Zealand bank (e.g., ANZ, ASB, BNZ, or Westpac) supervised by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Certificate of Incorporation, New Zealand Business Number, constitution, and the directors' resolution approving the bank account. Complete the bank's standard account-opening and signature mandates, and satisfy the customer due diligence requirements of the AML/CFT Act 2009 for all ultimate beneficial owners, including a declaration of source of funds and expected transaction profiles for SWIFT wire transfers and documentary letters of credit. After account opening, record the allotment of the initial shares in the company's share register, issue share certificates under section 90 of the Companies Act 1993, and lodge a copy in the statutory records.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Certificate of Registration issued by the Inland Revenue Department (IRD number certificate)
Company constitution
Board resolution approving account signatories
Passport copies of all beneficial owners
Ultimate beneficial ownership declaration and source-of-funds statement
Share register and share certificates (internal statutory records)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence because of the high-proof spirits trade, furnish a written compliance memorandum, the pending or issued wholesale liquor licence application number, and illustrative export invoices; execute any further AML/CFT attestation and, if the application is declined, approach an alternate registered bank with a strengthened KYC pack and reference from a licensed legal counsel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Wholesale Alcohol Licence and Customs Registered Exporter Status
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Licensing Committee of the relevant territorial authority; New Zealand Customs Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a complete application for an off-licence authorising the wholesale supply of alcohol under Part 2 of the Sale and Supply of Alcohol Act 2012, limiting supply to overseas licensed purchasers, New Zealand licensed retailers, and New Zealand licensed wholesalers in accordance with the proposed host responsibility policy. Publish the statutory public notice and serve copies on the New Zealand Police and the Medical Officer of Health as required. Concurrently, apply to the New Zealand Customs Service for registration as an exporter of classifiable spirits under the Customs and Excise Act 2018, identifying the relevant tariff classification (e.g., HS 2208.90 for baijiu), and, if bonded storage is intended, provide the schedule of the excise-licensed warehouse.
required_dossiers: Application for Off-Licence (Wholesale) in the form prescribed by the territorial authority
Certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation
Certified copy of the company constitution
Copy of the lease, title, or licence to occupy the licensed premises
Dimensioned floor plan of the storage and despatch facility
Host responsibility policy and proposed licence conditions
Fit and Proper Person questionnaire with New Zealand Police vetting consent
Customs Registered Exporter application and tariff classification statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the District Licensing Committee, Police, or Medical Officer of Health objects, the applicant may appear at a licensing hearing to adduce evidence of suitability under section 105 of the Sale and Supply of Alcohol Act 2012; a refusal may be appealed to the Alcohol Regulatory and Licensing Authority within 15 working days, and the licence scope may be narrowed to export-only transactions with enhanced record-keeping and CCTV conditions to address objections.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) in conjunction with the District Licensing Committee of the territorial authority under the Sale and Supply of Alcohol Act 2012, and the New Zealand Customs Service under the Customs and Excise Act 2018.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Off-Licence for Wholesale Supply of Spirits (Sale and Supply of Alcohol Act 2012) together with Registered Exporter Approval under the Customs and Excise Act 2018 for the export of high-proof sorghum baijiu.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA New Zealand), operating under the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms (HSNO) Act 1996 and the Resource Management Act 1991.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 - Low-risk registration; a full Environmental Impact Assessment is not required for a wholesale export operation without distillation or manufacturing. The operation must obtain an HSNO Location Compliance Certificate for any warehouse storing Class 3.1D flammable liquids (high-proof baijiu at or above 50% ABV) if the aggregated quantity exceeds the scheduled 1,000-litre threshold; operations below that threshold remain subject to a self-certified HSNO compliance record.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process wastewater discharge for a non-manufacturing exporter; primary containment and 110% bunding for all Class 3.1D flammable liquid storage; vapour and VOC exposure not exceeding the New Zealand Workplace Exposure Standard for ethanol of 1,000 ppm TWA (8-hour); fire-fighting water retention with no off-site discharge; compliance with the regional council's permitted-activity stormwater rule for premises drainage, including a sediment filter or oil-water separator if wheeled handling of full containers occurs.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety and Evacuation Scheme approval from Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) for premises storing flammable liquids; Building Code Compliance Certificate from the territorial authority confirming structural load ratings in accordance with the NZS 1170 structural design actions standard; occupation clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 issued through WorkSafe New Zealand for dangerous-good handling procedures, emergency response plans, first-aid provisions, and a documented hazardous-substances inventory under the HSNO regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand Government – official portal myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For NZ_LTD (a New Zealand-incorporated limited company), the Companies Office registration is completed first; the entity then applies to the IRD for an IRD number (the sole tax identification number used for income tax and GST) via myIR, submitting the certificate of incorporation, NZBN record, director details, registered office, and intended business activity. A non-resident company carrying on a taxable activity in NZ (or intending to do so) may also be registered by its approved agent using the IRD's non-resident company registration form (IR742) and GST registration application; the IRD issues the IRD/GST number, which must be quoted on all tax invoices. Registration for GST is compulsory when taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period; voluntary registration is available to exporters so that input GST can be recovered.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. NZ_LTD is a separate legal and taxable entity under New Zealand law; as a New Zealand resident company it is taxed on worldwide income at the 28% corporate rate, while the same entity is the registered GST person. The entity cannot be treated as a pass-through or disregarded entity for New Zealand tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style 'check-the-box' election or hybrid entity election exists in New Zealand. Statutory classification is determined by the Companies Act 1993 and the Income Tax Act 2007. Limited elections available: voluntary GST registration under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, GST grouping election under section 55, consolidated income tax group election under subpart FM of the Income Tax Act 2007, and financial arrangement timing elections. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are mandatory under the BEPS hybrid rules and cannot be waived by election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) – New Zealand value-added tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period (including zero-rated exports); voluntary registration is allowed for any person carrying on, or intending to carry on, a taxable activity in New Zealand.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: There is no real-time fiscal clearance or pre-approval requirement for GST invoices. New Zealand has adopted voluntary e-invoicing over the PEPPOL network (PEPPOL BIS 3.0); no API or digital stamping is mandated by Inland Revenue. All GST-registered suppliers must issue a tax invoice within 28 days of a request, containing the IRD number, supplier name and address, date of supply, description, GST-exclusive amount, GST amount, and (for supplies over NZD 1,000) the buyer's name and address. Export documentation is transmitted to New Zealand Customs electronically through the Trade Single Window, not for GST clearance purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of baijiu from New Zealand are zero-rated under section 11(1) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 when the supplier exports the goods (or delivers them to a carrier for export) within 28 days of the time of supply and holds sufficient documentary evidence of physical export. The zero-rating also requires the sale to be an unconditional supply to a non-resident customer, the goods must leave New Zealand, the supplier must retain customs and shipping records, and the proceeds must enter the New Zealand export stream. Domestic services, local warehousing, and any supply not proved to be exported are taxable at 15%; input GST credits can be refunded via the GST return once the zero-rated export is substantiated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs electronic Export Declaration (Trade Single Window clearance confirmation)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from New Zealand
Commercial invoice and packing list identifying the goods as Chinese baijiu and the ultimate export destination
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of export sale proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may audit zero-rating claims and require production of the export evidence bundle. If the goods are not exported within 28 days or the documentary trail is deficient, the supply is recharacterised as taxable at 15% GST, giving rise to increased assessments, use-of-money interest, and shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% for failing to take reasonable care or for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion. Input credits previously claimed on export-related purchases are clawed back when the corresponding export zero-rating fails. Records must generally be retained for 7 years. False export declarations may additionally trigger penalties and seizure under the Customs and Excise Act 2018. There is no statutory FX repatriation requirement in New Zealand; the 180-day benchmark is a commercial and pipeline control, and failure to receive proceeds within that period may be treated by IRD as evidence that no genuine export occurred.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) — central bank and prudential regulator; no separate foreign-exchange administration. AML/CFT supervision of banks is jointly exercised by the RBNZ and the Financial Markets Authority under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand has full current- and capital-account convertibility, consistent with IMF Article VIII obligations. There are no general exchange controls, prior-use restrictions, or profit-repatriation impediments; dividends, interest, trust distributions and capital proceeds may be converted and remitted freely in New Zealand dollars or any foreign currency, subject only to bank KYC/AML/CFT checks, tax withholding compliance, and the Overseas Investment Act 2005 where a transaction implicates sensitive New Zealand land or significant business assets. For a wholesale liquor exporter, no RBNZ consent is required for ordinary trade payments, loans, or equity subscriptions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. There is no statutory timeline for export proceeds surrender and no mandatory conversion ratio. A New Zealand exporter may retain export receipts indefinitely in foreign-currency bank accounts, use them to pay foreign suppliers, or convert to NZD at market-determined rates. The only obligations are record-keeping under the AML/CFT Act, tax treatment of foreign-currency gains/losses, and disclosure to bankers for source-of-funds and beneficial-ownership verification.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational NZD Account with segregated Foreign-Currency Sub-Accounts
Operational NZD Account plus Trade Finance and Loan Accounts
Everyday Business Account and Offshore/Import Working-Capital Facility
Business Transaction Account and FCY/Global Account suite
Business Account with Ancillary FX Services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium for primary NZD clearing but useful for secondary or fringe FX. Offshore digital EMIs and electronic-money institutions are not regulated deposit-takers in New Zealand and cannot provide local current-account or letter-of-credit facilities as if they were licensed banks. They may provide payment services only if registered on the Financial Service Providers Register and compliant with the FSP Act 2008 and AML/CFT obligations. Such providers are not suitable for the main NZD settlement or documentary trade operations; use a licensed New Zealand or Australian bank for core treasury. Non-bank EMIs such as global online payment firms can support ancillary supplier payments and low-value repatriations in CNY/USD/AUD corridors, but they are not a substitute for a regulated bank relationship for SWIFT MT103 and commercial LC transactions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand banks do not impose blanket physical attendance; remote onboarding is possible for local-registered companies with straightforward beneficial-ownership chains. However, for a newly incorporated NZ Ltd whose shareholders are non-resident, or whose control structure involves a foreign trust, banks commonly require: (i) a face-to-face or video interview with at least one director or authorized signatory; (ii) a locally resident director or registered office if the ultimate beneficial owner is in a higher-risk jurisdiction; and (iii) original or notarially certified corporate documents. For Chinese shareholder structures, expect bank-sanctioned enhanced due diligence, a physical visit by a bank compliance officer or in-person attestation in Auckland/Christchurch, remote video with independent verification, and a clear statement of anticipated transaction volumes for the Chinese-baijiu distribution business. In practice, a New Zealand resident director with signatory authority materially expedites opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident Chinese shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner located outside New Zealand with heightened sanctions-risk or source-of-wealth ambiguity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Certificate of Incorporation and Constitution of NZ_LTD; registered office and local director evidence; full corporate chart showing ultimate beneficial owners, passports/proof of identity; notarized directors and shareholders resolutions appointing signatories; bank reference letters from the Chinese investing institution; detailed source-of-wealth report for share subscription; audited source-of-funds files showing legitimate trading profits or verified personal assets; explanation of the Chinese investor's SAFE ODI registration certificate or outbound-permission documentation where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Alcohol distribution modelled as higher money-laundering or duty-evasion risk due to commercial nuance of spirits wholesale
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid New Zealand alcohol wholesale licence or statutory exemption analysis; export and import permits for each destination market; supplier contracts, invoices, and Bills of Lading covering the physical flow of Chinese Baijiu; excise and GST/fringe-tax filings showing duty already accounted; standard liquor-industry compliance manual; sales ledger and distributor agreements showing legitimate commercial rationale and arm's-length pricing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious use of a family trust or layered corporate structure to obscure control
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified deed of trust, trustee resolutions, trust register with details of settlor, trustees, discretionary objects and protector; a New Zealand trust's IRD number and foreign-trust registration certificate if applicable; narrative explaining commercial purpose of the trust in the baijiu export business; legal opinion from a New Zealand lawyer confirming beneficial ownership and absence of nominee or straw-man arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction-size mismatch where projected monthly USD/CNY/NDZ flows materially exceed the capital injected into the entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed distribution agreements with overseas wholesalers showing committed volumes and prices; warehouse and sub-storage agreements for high-proof spirits; supplier purchase orders from the Chinese distiller or export agent with 12-month forecast; bank statements or proof of credit facilities; management accounts projecting liquidity and inventory turnover; explanation of settlement terms including LC at sight, CAD, wire transfer, or 30-60 day terms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure on counterparties in the China-Hong Kong-NZ cross-border route and vague shipping lanes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening results of all counterparties, banks and vessels against OFAC, EU, UN and New Zealand sanctions lists; complete transportation chain with freight forwarders, carriers and container numbers; underlying commercial invoices, packing lists and certificates of origin proving physical goods and arm's-length valuation; compliance policy refusing cash or third-party payments, transshipment through sanctioned territories, and split invoicing; acknowledgement that non-documentary payments require prior bank approval.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound equity subscriptions from the Chinese shareholder must be routed by SWIFT wire (MT103) to the NZ_LTD NZD bank account with a clear purpose code such as '112 - Equity Investment' or the bank's equivalent BoP classification, using the exact legal name shown in the New Zealand Companies Register. The remitter must ensure the Chinese outward remittance is lawful under Chinese foreign-exchange law, including SAFE cross-border ODI registration if the Chinese shareholder holds 10%+ of the shares and is investing equity rather than making trade pre-payment. For the NZ receiving bank, deliver a board resolution authorizing the capital raise, updated share register and Companies Office filings confirming 'Shares Issued for Cash', share subscription letters, invoicing if applicable, source-of-wealth statements, and confirmation that no funds are remitted on behalf of unrelated third parties. Shareholder loans should be documented with written loan agreements, interest and repayment terms, and arm's-length pricing to prevent tax and thin-capitalization disputes. New Zealand does not require RBNZ approval for inbound equity, but the bank will apply AML/CFT verification before accepting principal.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements in the Chinese-baijiu supply chain should settle through: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier and agent payments in CNY/USD/EUR, with payment references containing the commercial invoice number and product description; (ii) Commercial Irrevocable Letters of Credit using SWIFT MT700/MT720, with MT754 advising negotiation, for larger Chinese distiller or trading-house transactions; and (iii) documentary collections or electronic-BPO platforms for moderate-value repeat transactions. For sales to overseas distributors, NZ_LTD should request inbound payments via SWIFT MT103 with invoice purpose, or receive payment by LC at sight. Where CNY settlement is preferred, the clearing rail should be CIPS through a participating Chinese bank, while legacy USD wires remain on Fedwire or CHIPS via the NZ bank's US correspondent. All instructions must be screened against sanctions lists and include the full invoice, packing list, Bill of Lading, certificate of origin, and health/liquor export certificates. The NZ bank may require a declaration of the ultimate beneficiary name and country for each outgoing transaction and will generally refuse third-party-payment consignees.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla foreign-exchange forwards on NZD/USD, NZD/CNY, NZD/AUD and USD/CNY, subject to corporate FX policy and governance approval
Vanilla FX options, both puts and calls, used solely for hedging forecast cash flows and inventory purchase commitments
Cross-currency swaps between NZD, USD, CNY, AUD and EUR for balance-sheet liquidity transformation and alignment of debt-service currencies with operating cash flows

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies in which onshore deliverability is restricted or illiquid, executed only through a licensed counterparty and documented as hedges of recognized commercial exposures
FX target-maturity forwards and forwards with pick-up payments, approved only where the bank confirms hedge accounting treatment and no speculative leverage is involved

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of a Limited Company (statutory confirmation of registered office, directors, members, and significant controllers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 10 working days after the annual return date, being the anniversary of incorporation unless an alternative annual return date has been approved by the Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Repeated non-filing attracts an infringement notice; after a Registrar compliance notice and a further 20 working days without filing, the company may be struck off the Companies Register under s 318(1)(d) of the Companies Act 1993; reinstatement under ss 329-330 requires a court order, remedial filings, and payment of outstanding fees and penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Significant Controllers Register annual confirmation of UBO details for every individual holding 25% or more beneficial ownership or control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), MBIE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, aligned with the annual return due date; any change in significant controllers during the year must be notified within 10 working days after the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separate fee for the confirmation; failure to maintain and update the significant controllers register is an offence under the significant controllers disclosure regime, enforceable by infringement notices or fines, and persistent non-compliance may be treated as an unfiled annual return leading to strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: IR4 Company Income Tax Return (including Working Taxable Income Statement) e-filed via myIR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD / Te Tari Taake)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 7th day of the 7th month after the balance date (e.g., 7 July following a 31 March balance date); e-filed returns may receive an automatic one-month extension to 7 August if no outstanding return obligations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late Filing Penalty of NZ$200 immediately plus NZ$50 per day thereafter to a maximum of NZ$2,000 per return under the Tax Administration Act 1994, plus use-of-money interest on any unpaid terminal tax.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit is mandatory for FMC reporting entities (publicly accountable companies) and for non-FMC companies classified as large: total assets exceeding NZ$30 million or total revenue exceeding NZ$15 million. A small private liquor export wholesale company below those thresholds is exempt from audit unless shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares request an audit or the company constitution requires one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand IFRS (Tier 1) for large and publicly accountable entities; NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (Tier 2) for entities without public accountability; XRB Simplified Reporting Standards (Tier 3/4) for smaller for-profit entities. All frameworks constitute New Zealand generally accepted accounting practice (NZ GAAP).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members within 10 working days of lodgement. A company must maintain a Significant Controllers Register identifying any person with 25% or more ownership or control, and the significant controller details must be confirmed annually as part of the annual return. Any change during the year, including a share transfer that alters beneficial ownership, must be filed with the Registrar within 10 working days of the change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (records of board and shareholder meetings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 160 - 550 per annum (approx. NZD 250 - 850) as the typical New Zealand market range for registered office and registered agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - 18,000 (approx. NZD 10,000 - 30,000) for a certified audit of a small to mid-sized liquor export wholesaler if an audit is required; not incurred where the company qualifies for audit exemption

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
